title: Extinct intermediates connect each species to a common progenitor, not to each other

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Extinct intermediates connect each species to a common progenitor, not to each other

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The extinct intermediate forms required by descent with modification link each species to a common, usually unknown, progenitor, and that progenitor will generally have differed in some respects from all of its modified descendants, so forms directly intermediate between two living species should not be expected.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IX: On the Imperfection of the Geological Record

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: we should always look for forms intermediate between each species and a common but unknown progenitor; and the progenitor will generally have differed in some respects from all its modified descendants.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter IX, “On the Imperfection of the Geological Record”; section “On the nature of extinct intermediate varieties; on their number”. Scope: all pairs of related species, living or extinct

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch09-01: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.78

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The branching rather than ladder-like prediction is directly testable across many well-sampled clades. Public phylogenetic and fossil data are extensive, though ancestral identity remains probabilistic.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For related living species, infer their common ancestor on independent phylogenies and test whether fossil or reconstructed intermediates lie along separate stem lineages rather than morphologically midway between the living tips. The predicted branching pattern supports the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
True ancestors are rarely identifiable as such.

Fossil sampling is uneven.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.76
data adequacy: 0.68
discriminating power: 0.72
data existence: 0.91
operationalizability: 0.8

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Occurrences, matrices, and trees are public and sufficient for a geometric test in a minority of clades. That is a restricted-scope proxy for a claim about all related species, most of which lack fossils. Discriminating power is moderate because off-midpoint ancestors are also produced by rate variation, not only by the branching structure Darwin described.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In well-fossilized clades, place fossils and reconstructed ancestors in morphospace relative to living species pairs. Ancestors and fossils that lie off the straight line between two living species, and that connect each species to an earlier node, support the prediction; a surplus of fossils that are direct morphological intermediates between living species would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Unequal rates of change move ancestors off the midpoint even when the path was a direct bridge.

Multidimensional morphology makes 'directly intermediate' ambiguous.

Only clades with dense fossils and coded characters can be used.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data existence: 0.74
operationalizability: 0.62
discriminating power: 0.52
data adequacy: 0.42
